clue.text: Travelled round in American ballet

parts.note: travelled, as on horseback, means rode
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone toured inside a ballet from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here, not a container signal. The ballet is Aaron Copland's cowboy ballet of 1942.
explanation.definitionFit: Copland's 1942 cowboy ballet carries this title, so it is an American ballet by name.

clue.text: Chairman of Royal Commission?

parts.note: read as an academic holding a university chair created by royal appointment, not the head of an inquiry

explanation.surface: Who heads a royal commission of inquiry?
explanation.walkthrough: A university professorship is a chair, so the holder of a chair founded by the Crown is its chairman.
explanation.definitionFit: Regius chairs at old British universities were founded by the monarch, so their holders hold a royally commissioned chair.

clue.text: Refuse to let daughter join seaman

parts.note: Sir James Clark Ross was a British naval officer and polar explorer

explanation.surface: A father won't allow his daughter to marry a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless matter, rubbish or waste.

clue.text: Herb's treacherous daughter falls in love repeatedly

indicators.note: falls in says the daughter drops between the two letters for love
repeatedly means the letter for love appears twice

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
Regan is one of King Lear's two treacherous daughters

explanation.surface: A herb's disloyal daughter keeps falling in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb's' is read as Herb is: the definition plus a link. 'falls in' places REGAN between two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a Mediterranean culinary herb related to marjoram.

clue.text: Cooks a little plant

parts.note: to devil food is to cook it with hot spices, so cooks means devils
a little means a bit

explanation.surface: Chefs prepare a small portion of some vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' looks like a noun for chefs but is a verb: devilled kidneys are cooked with hot seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil's-bit scabious is a meadow wildflower with blue heads, a named plant.

clue.text: Mysterious vessel at Land's End

indicators.note: End picks the final letter of Land's

parts.note: Noah's ark is a vessel

explanation.surface: A strange ship lies off Land's End in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the far western tip of Cornwall, England; here it means the last letter of 'Land's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dark is obscure or hidden, as in dark secrets, so mysterious.

clue.text: Variant one century old could be found in such a collection

definitions.text: Variant one century old could be found in such a collection

indicators.text: could be found in such a collection
indicators.note: a collection gathers items together in any order, so these letters are assembled anew

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I
C is the abbreviation for century, a hundred

explanation.surface: An antique dating from a hundred years ago belongs in a collection of period items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection' gathers VARIANT, I, C and O as a pool to rearrange; the whole clue also describes a set of nineteenth-century objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoriana are objects from Queen Victoria's reign, which a century-old variant piece could join.

clue.text: Action against workers philosopher pronounced unacceptable

indicators.note: pronounced says the philosopher's name is taken by its spoken form

parts.note: John Locke was an English philosopher
out means not allowed, as in that's out

explanation.surface: A philosopher declared industrial action against workers unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCKE spoken sounds the same as LOCK, the spelling the grid needs.
explanation.definitionFit: In a lockout an employer shuts staff out of the workplace, a measure taken against employees.

clue.text: Type who eats foie gras made from high-quality liver

parts.note: bon is French for good
a viveur is one who lives, a liver, in French

explanation.surface: A gourmet eats pâté made from top-grade liver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liver' looks like the organ in foie gras; it means one who lives, rendered in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon viveur enjoys luxurious food and drink, the kind of person who eats goose-liver pâté.

clue.text: It's not so attractive as a habit, getting drunk

definitions.text: It's not so attractive as a habit
definitions.meaning: a habit is a garment, so one that is less attractive is one shabbier through use
drunk means intoxicated, the worse for drink

explanation.surface: Drinking is an unattractive habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' looks like a custom but is a garment, such as a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means shabby from long use, and also tipsy or intoxicated.

clue.text: Showing, regular patterns encountered in poem — good only at the beginning

indicators.note: in signals that the word for encountered goes inside the trimmed poem
the word for the poem is to keep its first G but lose the later one, so the letter for good stays only at the start

parts.note: a georgic is a poem about farming, like Virgil's Georgics
encountered means met

explanation.surface: A design with regular shapes appears in a poem, and the poem is good only at its start.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgil's Georgics are the model for the georgic, a poem on farming; the clue lets its good keep only the opening G.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometric designs are built from regular lines and shapes, so they display regular patterns.

clue.text: Story that may be used in making a picture

definitions.meaning: the French word for a short story or tale, used in English for that literary form

definitions.text: that may be used in making a picture
definitions.meaning: a hard crayon of graphite and clay, named after its French inventor and used by artists for drawing

explanation.surface: A tale which might be adapted into a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picture' suggests a film, but the second sense is a drawing made with a Conté crayon.
explanation.definitionFit: A short tale in French literary usage, and a brand of drawing crayon named after its inventor Conté.

clue.text: Remove Austen's novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of the author's name take a new order

parts.note: the six letters of the novelist's surname, the possessive adding none

explanation.surface: Take away one of Jane Austen's books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun for one of her books but is the adjective signalling a fresh arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To unseat someone is to remove them from a seat or position, as in an election.

clue.text: Engagement ring composer has on

indicators.note: has on says the composer wears the ring, so the letter for it follows his name

parts.note: Alexander Borodin was a Russian composer
a ring is round, the letter O

explanation.surface: A composer is wearing an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement ring' reads as one phrase, but 'Engagement' is the definition: the 1812 battle outside Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: Borodino was the great battle of Napoleon's 1812 Russian campaign, and a battle is a military engagement.

clue.text: Who is, possibly, attached to male in republic?

definitions.text: Who is, possibly, attached to male in republic?

indicators.note: attached to says the word for male is joined on after the rearranged letters

parts.note: IR is the abbreviation for the Irish Republic

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters may take another form, so who is is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a man is a male

explanation.surface: Who might be married to a man in a republic?
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges WHO IS into ISHWO; IR goes first and MAN is attached at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A female citizen of Ireland is the woman of that republic, possibly married to a man there.

clue.text: Special port I decant into mixture

indicators.note: into says the word for decant goes inside the rearranged letters
special suggests something made differently, so the letters of port and I are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to decant wine is to pour it

explanation.surface: A host decants a special port into some blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decant' looks like an instruction for the port, but it supplies its own letters, poured into the shuffled port and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a scented blend of dried petals, and by extension any medley or miscellany.

clue.text: Achieving good results with the box camera

definitions.text: Achieving good results with the box camera

parts.words: Achieving good results with the box camera
parts.note: read as looking good on television, the box, rather than taking good snaps with a simple box camera

explanation.surface: Getting fine photos with an old box camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box camera' suggests the old Kodak box; 'the box' is slang for television, and the camera is a TV one.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegenic person looks attractive on television screens.

clue.text: Longs to protect members of clan

definitions.text: Longs to protect members of clan

parts.words: Longs to protect members of clan
parts.note: longs are long trousers, and the members protected are the legs of Scottish clansmen in tartan

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to guard the people of a Scottish clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Longs' looks like a verb of yearning; it is a noun for long trousers, and 'members' are limbs, not clansmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Trews are close-fitting tartan trousers worn in the Scottish Highlands, covering the legs of a clansman.

clue.text: Traveller taking turn around end of liner's deck

indicators.note: around says the turned name surrounds that letter
taking a turn means the traveller's name faces the other way

parts.note: Marco Polo was the famous Venetian traveller

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of liner's

explanation.surface: A voyager takes a stroll around the end of a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking turn' turns POLO into OLOP, and 'around' wraps it round R, the last letter of 'liner's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Writer, female

parts.note: a poet is a writer
the suffix -ess marks a female, as in lioness

explanation.surface: A woman author.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetess is an old term for a woman who writes verse.

clue.text: Simple type Society treated with fairness

indicators.note: treated suggests something processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plain sort of club handled matters with even-handedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' means a printing typeface, not a kind of person; 'treated' rearranges FAIRNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sans-serif typeface lacks the small strokes at letter ends, so it is a plain style of print.

clue.text: In strait, vessel initially kept afloat

indicators.note: In places the letter inside the strait
kept says the strait holds the letter within it

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of vessel

explanation.surface: In a narrow channel, a ship at first stayed afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afloat' looks literal but means financially sound; the Solent is the strait off Southampton.
explanation.definitionFit: A business kept afloat is solvent, able to pay its debts.

clue.text: Creature with excellent vision and wisdom?

parts.note: the eagle is proverbial for keen sight, as in eagle-eyed
the owl is the proverbial emblem of wisdom

explanation.surface: An animal blessed with sharp eyes and great sagacity.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle owl is a large owl species of Europe and Asia, an animal.

clue.text: One's powerless to take flight

parts.note: read as a craft with no engine power that nevertheless flies, rather than someone unable to run away

explanation.surface: Someone is unable to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take flight' suggests fleeing; it means flying, and 'powerless' means without an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider is an aircraft flying without an engine, so it flies without power.

clue.text: Resting-place for Duke, a grand one

parts.note: Ivan III was Grand Duke of Moscow, so a grand duke can be Ivan

explanation.surface: A bed for a duke, and an impressive one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a grand one' reads as praise for the bed but means a grand duke, here Ivan.
explanation.definitionFit: A divan is a low bed or couch, somewhere to rest.

clue.text: Just possible? Extremely likely!

parts.note: on means feasible, as in that plan isn't on

indicators.note: Extremely picks the first and last letters of likely

explanation.surface: Just possible? More like very probable!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just possible' reads as one phrase, but 'Just' is the definition, meaning merely.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only both mean merely, as in only a child.

clue.text: Witness trapping partners in hearing, perhaps

indicators.note: trapping says the word for witness holds the partners inside it

parts.note: to witness is to see
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A witness catching two accomplices at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court session but is the definition: one of the five faculties. N and S are bridge partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing is one example of the bodily faculties of perception, like sight or touch.

clue.text: Equivalent of piecework for engineer

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
oeuvre is French for work, used in English for an artist's body of work

explanation.surface: What equals piece-rate pay for an engineer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equivalent of' asks for words matching each half of 'piecework'; 'engineer' is a verb meaning contrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer an outcome is to contrive it by skilful scheming, which is to manoeuvre.

clue.text: Refusal to accept service charge

parts.note: read as refusing to attend church services, once a criminal charge in England, rather than declining a restaurant tip

explanation.surface: A diner won't pay the service charge on the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service charge' looks like a restaurant extra; the service is a church one, and refusing to attend was once an offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Recusants refused to attend Church of England services, an offence punished by fines.

clue.text: Our top authority on fashion cosmetic

indicators.note: on says the Queen's letters come after the word for fashion

parts.note: ton is an old word for fashion or high society
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, Britain's highest authority

explanation.surface: Britain's monarch is the leading judge of style in face creams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'authority on fashion' reads as one phrase, but 'on' only orders the pieces; ton is an old word for the fashionable world.
explanation.definitionFit: Toner is a skin lotion applied in beauty routines, a cosmetic.
